name: Microneedling under eyes

lead: Microneedling, formally collagen induction therapy, repeatedly punctures the skin with tiny sterile needles. Appearance forums discuss it for the under-eye area, where skin is thin and people look for texture and tone improvement.
Published research on microneedling covers scarring, acne and hair loss among other uses, but none of the registered studies reviewed here focus on the under-eye area.

paras: The cosmetic rationale is that controlled micro-injury prompts the skin to repair itself and produce collagen. Wikipedia's article does not itself explain the mechanism.

Health officials have warned about infection risk when microneedling is combined with platelet-rich plasma ("vampire facials") in non-medical settings; in April 2024 the CDC reported three HIV diagnoses among patients of one New Mexico spa [1].

lead: Microneedling, also called collagen induction therapy, dermarolling or skin needling, is a cosmetic procedure in which tiny sterile needles repeatedly puncture the skin [1]. In looksmaxxing discussion it is applied to the under-eye area for thin, crepey or discolored skin.

Reported uses of microneedling include scarring and acne, and some studies suggest adding minoxidil improves hair-loss treatment versus minoxidil alone [1]. The benefit of combining it with platelet-rich plasma remains unproven according to Wikipedia [1].
No studies focused on microneedling under the eyes were found, so evidence for this specific use is limited.

paras: Microneedling is distinguished from other uses of microneedle devices such as transdermal drug delivery and vaccination [1]. Devices described include stamps and dermarollers [1]. Radiofrequency variants combine needling with heat energy for facial rejuvenation.

Wikipedia reports health-official warnings that platelet-rich plasma facials performed by people without infection-control training could spread blood-borne infections, citing three HIV diagnoses among patients of one Albuquerque spa reported in April 2024 [1].

No studies found on microneedling specifically under the eyes. Registered trials on other conditions include a radiofrequency microneedling study for facial photoaging and wrinkles with a post-procedure cream [2] and a comparison of dermatological approaches for melasma [3].
